title: A finite affine morphism admits a finite section-covered ambient scheme
statement: Let $f:Y\to X$ be a finite morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] of schemes with $X$ affine [def-pc-scheme]. There exist an affine scheme $X\prime$, a surjective finite locally free morphism $a:X\prime\to X$ [def-weil-surjective-morphism, def-pc-finite-locally-free], an affine scheme $W$, and a finite locally free morphism $p:W\to X\prime$, together with a closed immersion $j:Y\prime=Y\times_X X\prime\hookrightarrow W$ over $X\prime$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-closed-immersion]. There is a finite family of closed subschemes $W_k\hookrightarrow W$ whose underlying sets cover $W$, and each restriction $p|_{W_k}:W_k\to X\prime$ is an isomorphism. The projection $Y\prime\to Y$ is also surjective finite locally free. No Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 03HW, label lemma-massage-finite, clauses (1)-(5); affineness of X\prime and W follows from the finite morphisms in the same statement.

proof.text: Use global sections of the affine schemes X and Y. Finite module generators generate the algebra; finite-algebra integrality supplies monic equations for them. No positive-degree modification or nonempty-spectrum case split is needed.

Apply simultaneous faithful finite free splitting to the equations. The finite-free spectrum lemma gives finite local freeness of Spec S -> Spec R. Faithfulness and finite-algebra integrality give spectrum surjectivity by lying over. Compose with the affine comparison isomorphism to get a: Xprime -> X.

Let C be the tensor product over S of the AdjoinRoot algebras of the mapped equations. The monic tensor presentation theorem supplies its finite basis. Its evaluation at 1 tensor x_i is surjective: the equations vanish by coefficient base change, and the base-changed generators generate S tensor_R B by Mathlib adjoin_one_tmul_image_eq_top. The finite-free spectrum lemma gives p:Spec C -> Spec S finite locally free.

The tensor-product pushout gives a pullback square of spectra. Transport it by X.isoSpec and Y.isoSpec to identify Spec(S tensor_R B) with the actual pullback of f and a. Applying Spec to the surjective evaluation map and precomposing with this comparison gives the closed immersion j. Algebra-map compatibility proves j followed by p is the second projection.

Apply the split monic tensor section-cover theorem. Every evaluation e_k:C -> S is surjective and fixes S, so Spec(e_k) is a closed immersion whose composite with p is the identity. The prime-spectrum covering assertion is exactly the required pointwise finite cover.

The first pullback projection is the base change of a. Mathlib base-change instances preserve its surjectivity, finiteness, flatness and local finite presentation. Assemble the last three properties into IsFiniteLocallyFree.

lean.statement: theorem exists_finite_affine_section_cover {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X) [IsFinite f] [IsAffine X] : ∃ (X' : Scheme.{u}) (a : X' ⟶ X), IsAffine X' ∧ Surjective a ∧ a.IsFiniteLocallyFree ∧ ∃ (W : Scheme.{u}) (p : W ⟶ X') (j : pullback f a ⟶ W), IsAffine W ∧ p.IsFiniteLocallyFree ∧ IsClosedImmersion j ∧ j ≫ p = pullback.snd f a ∧ (∃ (n : ℕ) (Z : Fin n → Scheme.{u}) (i : ∀ k : Fin n, Z k ⟶ W), (∀ k : Fin n, IsClosedImmersion (i k) ∧ IsIso (i k ≫ p)) ∧ ∀ w : W, ∃ (k : Fin n) (z : Z k), i k z = w) ∧ Surjective (pullback.fst f a) ∧ (pullback.fst f a).IsFiniteLocallyFree
